Version 0.4.2 fixes a bug that could leave a file stuck in conflict on a receive-only machine, and adds a way to take the incoming version of a conflict.

A receiver applies changes in batches. It renames each received file into place, then records the whole batch in its index with one commit. If the daemon stopped between those two steps, the files were in place but the index didn't know about them. A service stop does that easily, because the process exits within about 80 ms. So does a crash, a folder pause, a dropped connection or an error. The next scan then saw a changed file and recorded it as an edit made on the receiver. On a receive-only folder that edit is never sent back to the source, so every later version of the file became a conflict. I hit this restarting my Linux receiver during the 0.4.1 upgrade. A SQLite database that a scheduler rewrites every minute collected 102 conflict copies before I paused the folder.

Now each incoming version is recorded before anything is published, and the record is removed in the batch's own commit. If a batch never commits, the next scan or retry finds the matching file and indexes it as the peer's version.

`ysync conflict resolve --take-incoming FOLDER ID` is new. Stop the daemon and pick the record. ysync verifies the preserved incoming file, puts it in place and archives your local version under `.ysync/versions`. On a receive-only folder it also drops the receiver's own version counter, so later source versions apply normally again. Use it once on any path an earlier version already left stuck. If a newer incoming version of the same path is pending, the command names it so you can take the newest one.

The index gains one table, created on first start. Nothing changes on the wire or in configuration, so 0.4.x peers synchronize with each other and you can upgrade one machine at a time. But stopping a 0.4.1 receiver mid-batch can still cause this one last time, so upgrade the receiving machine while the sender is stopped or idle. Run `brew update && brew upgrade ysync`, then `brew services restart ysync`. Cargo users can install tag `v0.4.2`. Experimental prerelease.
